newsitem.title: UK: Copper under new pressure in late London.
newsitem.headline: Copper under new pressure in late London.

text.p: Copper prices remained under pressure in late London inter-office activity barely holding support at $1,920 per tonne by 1800 GMT when Comex closed.

Declines under $2,000 had been extended significantly earlier during the day so that three months copper finished the kerb at $1,925. This was down $95 a tonne from Wednesday. Later activity was desultory but copper stayed pressured.
Three-months only just clung to the $1,920 value and was assessed at $1,916/1,920 just after 1800 GMT.

Next resistance is seen at $1,900 whilst next direction may come from LME stocks data due on Friday. "The market is now in need of some more fundamental direction, which the LME stocks should hopefully provide," brokers Rudolf Wolff said in their Evening Metal Report. "The recent failed upside break is likely to lead to an ever increasing eagerness by producers to sell into strength". Aluminium which had crumbled under $1,500 with copper was at 1800GMT bid at $1,490. It had ended the kerb at $1,492, down $16.
